card.stem: A dwelling house has a 400 mm external concrete block wall with a 200 mm full-fill insulated cavity. The ground floor is an insulated concrete floor with a 20 mm floating tongue-and-groove hardwood finish, as shown.
card.questionText: To a scale of 1:5, draw a vertical section through the strip foundation, the external wall and the ground floor. Show the typical construction details from the bottom of the foundation to a level 400 mm above finished floor. Show the position of the radon barrier and include four typical dimensions on your drawing. Show 1.0 metre width of floor.

rows.verbatim: Any 9 of the above details ( 4 marks each)
rows.contextNote: Credit the best NINE acceptable details at 4 marks each, capped at 36. Marked details: 100 mm concrete path/ground level; DPC; 100 mm block outer leaf and 19 mm render; full-fill cavity insulation; wall tie; 100 mm block inner leaf and 13 mm plaster; skirting board; 20 mm floating timber floor; 150 mm concrete floor taped and sealed to the wall; 300 mm floor insulation; DPM/radon barrier; hardcore and sand blinding; concrete fill/foundation blocks; reinforced concrete foundation.
Four appropriate typical dimensions on the section, 1 each.

rows.contextNote: Such as: the greatest heat loss, up to 30%, is through the roof; the most effective way to save energy.

card.stem: The sketch shows a wood burning stove which is combined with a solar collector to provide hot water for a dwelling house. Also shown are a dual-coil hot water cylinder and the expansion tank in the attic.

card.questionText: Outline two specific safety precautions to be observed in the Construction Studies room in each of the following situations: using a scalpel to cut modelling card; carrying a chisel; using a contact adhesive.

rows.verbatim: Using a scalpel to cut modelling card
rows.contextNote: Two precautions, 4 each. Such as: a clean flat surface and cutting mat; a firmly held straight edge; always cut away from your hands; score lightly then repeat; cover scalpels and replace blunt blades.
Two precautions, 4 each. Such as: carry it down by your side with the edge towards the floor; never in a pocket; walk, never run.
Two precautions, 4 each. Such as: latex gloves and goggles; a well-ventilated area; avoid inhaling the fumes; keep away from heat; follow the instructions for use and storage.

card.questionText: Explain, with the aid of notes and freehand sketches, any five of the following: lever valve; mortice and tenon joint; cob wall; thermal bridge; dual flush toilet; smart meter; solar gain; low-e glazing; access ramp.

rows.contextNote: Explain any five of the nine terms. Each term is marked separately: primary communication of relevant information 6 and other communication 4, in notes or sketches (the scheme reserves no fixed split between them). Lever valve: controls the flow of water with a single lever operating a hollow ball; the lever shows the valve open when parallel to the pipe and closed when perpendicular; a good seal; various diameters. Mortice and tenon joint: used in doors, windows and furniture: a mortice cut in one piece and a tenon, about a third of the thickness, formed on the end of the other to fit it. Cob wall: clay, straw or hemp mixed with water (sometimes lime or sand), built in layers on a coursed stone base, each layer dried before the next; tapered and finished with lime render. Thermal bridge: a bridge in the insulation, at floors, cills, lintels, jambs or roofs, conducting heat out; higher heat loss, condensation and mould; prevented by continuous insulation. Dual flush toilet: a cistern with two buttons: about 6–9 litres for solid and 3–4 litres for liquid waste, cutting water use and the water sent to treatment. Smart meter: records and shows the electricity used in the home and its cost, giving the householder control; may be topped up; can also record water or gas. Solar gain: free heat from solar radiation entering through glazing, stored in masonry as a heat sink; maximised by orientation, insulation and airtightness; the main principle of passive design. Low-e glazing: a thin transparent metal or metal-oxide coating on the panes that reflects heat back into the house while admitting solar gain; dearer but reduces heat loss. Access ramp: a sloping path for easy access for wheelchairs, buggies and people with restricted mobility: gradient about 1:20, at least 1500 mm clear width, sections no longer than 9.0 m, non-slip and well lit.
